items.title: Section: Eleven Objects of Confusion, and Five Kinds of Foolish Beings

items.zh: 於不現見義而生迷惑，是無明業。如是於現見義、劣義、中義、勝義、利益義、不利益義、真義、邪義、因義、果義而生迷惑，是無明業。又有十種愚癡有情，遍攝愚癡諸有情類。一、缺減愚癡，二、狂亂愚癡，三、散亂愚癡，四、自性愚癡，五、執著愚癡，六、迷亂愚癡，七、堅固愚癡，八、增上愚癡，九、無所了別愚癡，十、現見愚癡。缺減愚癡者，謂如有一，或缺於眼、或缺於耳，於眼所識色、耳所識聲一切境界皆不領解，是故愚癡。狂亂愚癡者，謂如有一，或遭逼迫、或遭大苦、或遭重病、或痛所切、或復顛癎令心狂亂。由此不了善作、惡作，是故愚癡。散亂愚癡者，謂如有一，心散異境，不能了餘善作、惡作，是故愚癡。自性愚癡者，謂如有一，於生死中無始以來，自性不了苦集滅道、眾生無我、法無我等，是故愚癡。執著愚癡者，謂如有一，墮外道中，彼於身見、身見為本諸見趣中不能解了，是故愚癡。
items.en: Generating confusion regarding what is not directly perceived is ignorance's function. Likewise generating confusion regarding what is directly perceived, the inferior, middling, and superior realms, the beneficial and harmful, the true and the false, and cause and result, is ignorance's function. There are also ten kinds of foolish being, fully covering every kind of foolish being there is. First, deficiency-foolishness, belonging to one lacking an eye or an ear, unable to understand any object at all, whether form known by the eye or sound known by the ear, and so foolish. Second, madness-foolishness, belonging to one whose mind is driven to derangement by pressure, great suffering, grave illness, sharp pain, or epilepsy, unable to distinguish wholesome from unwholesome action, and so foolish. Third, distraction-foolishness, belonging to one whose mind scatters to another object, unable to complete a wholesome or unwholesome act with genuine understanding, and so foolish. Fourth, intrinsic foolishness, belonging to one who, since beginningless time in birth and death, has by nature never understood suffering, origination, cessation, the path, or the selflessness of beings and dharmas, and so is foolish. Fifth, attachment-foolishness, belonging to one fallen among outsiders, unable to understand self-view and the views rooted in it, and so foolish.

items.title: Section: A Torch Spun Into a Wheel — And the Fool Who Never Expects to Age

items.zh: 迷亂愚癡者，謂如有一，或名想亂、或形量亂、或色相亂、或業用亂，於亂處法不能解了，是故愚癡。堅固愚癡者，謂如有一，畢竟無有般涅槃法，所有愚癡自性堅固，乃至諸佛亦不能拔。增上愚癡者，謂如有一，常恒無間習諸邪行，又邪行因所生眾苦之所逼切，雖知雖見，而故奔趣樂著嬉戲；或復貪等行者，亦是增上愚癡。無所解了愚癡者，謂如有一，不聞不思不修習故，於法於義不能解了，是故愚癡。現見愚癡者，謂如有一，現見諸行皆悉無常，而起常想；現見皆苦，而起樂想；現見不淨，而起淨想；現見無我，而起我想；現見病法、老法、死法，起安隱想，無逼惱想。
items.en: Confusion-foolishness belongs to one confused by perceptual, dimensional, coloristic, or functional illusion, unable to understand the deluded matter, and so foolish. Firm foolishness belongs to one utterly without the potential for final nirvana, their own foolish nature fixed so firmly that not even the buddhas can uproot it. Excessive foolishness belongs to one who constantly, without interruption, practices wrong conduct, and though pressed by the very suffering that wrong conduct produces, and though fully aware and fully seeing it, still races towards it in delighted indulgence; one given over to greed and the like is likewise excessively foolish. Non-comprehending foolishness belongs to one who, neither hearing, reflecting, nor practising, cannot understand the teaching or its meaning, and so is foolish. Foolishness in the face of direct perception belongs to one who, directly witnessing that all conditioned things are impermanent, still conceives them as permanent; witnessing that they are suffering, still conceives them as pleasant; witnessing impurity, still conceives purity; witnessing selflessness, still conceives a self; and witnessing sickness, old age, and death, still conceives security, free of any oppressive affliction.

items.title: Section: Three Degrees of Ignorance, and Darkness Across the Three Realms

items.zh: 又此無明，於五處所能為障礙。一、能障礙真實智喜，二、能障礙煩惱滅得，三、能障礙聖道成滿，四、能障礙往於善趣，五、能障礙世間現法諸吉祥事。問：何等名無明法？答：或有由無明故，墮無明趣，說名愚癡；非癡所嬈，不為癡垢，非癡所媚。謂住隨眠無明。或有愚癡，為癡所嬈，不為癡垢，非癡所媚。謂由纏所攝無明。或有愚癡，為癡所嬈，為癡所垢，非癡所媚。謂由發業無明發惡業已，於此惡行而生羞恥。或有愚癡，為癡所嬈，為癡所垢，為癡所媚。謂因無明發起種種惡不善業，於此惡行無有羞恥。此中由前三種，說名愚癡，墮無明趣，不名癡人。由後一種，說名癡人。或有闇法無明，謂在欲界；或有昧法無明，謂在色界；或有翳法無明，謂在無色界。
items.en: This ignorance obstructs beings in five places. First, it obstructs the joy of genuine wisdom. Second, it obstructs the attainment of affliction's cessation. Third, it obstructs the completion of the noble path. Fourth, it obstructs rebirth in the fortunate destinies. Fifth, it obstructs auspicious worldly circumstances in this very life. What is called the dharma of ignorance? Answer: some, on account of ignorance, fall into the class of the foolish, called foolish, yet are not troubled by foolishness, not stained by its impurity, and not seduced by it — this refers to dwelling in dormant ignorance alone. Of these, the first three kinds are called foolish, falling into the class of the foolish, yet not called a foolish person. Only the last is called a foolish person. There is a darkness-dharma ignorance, belonging to the desire realm; a dimness-dharma ignorance, belonging to the form realm; and a cataract-dharma ignorance, belonging to the formless realm.

items.title: Section: Ignorance's Cause and Fruit — The First Link Now Complete

items.zh: 因，如本地分已說。果，謂一切後有支。又於真如及諸諦義不能解了。或復猶豫，或即於此生邪決定。謂於諦理或增、或減，顛倒執著無常等故；或由增上慢故；或由自輕蔑
items.en: Its cause is as already explained in the Basic Section. Its fruit is every subsequent link of existence. Also, with respect to suchness and the meaning of the truths, either an inability to understand, or lingering doubt, or a wrongly settled conviction, arises. This is because of a distorted, exaggerating or diminishing grasp of impermanence and the rest; or because of overreaching conceit; or because of self-deprecation.

items.title: Section: Why Scripture Calls the Eye a Cause When the Seed Is the True Cause

items.zh: 故。餘有支決擇文，更不復現。復次，如世尊言：眼為因，色為緣，眼識得生；乃至身為因，觸為緣，身識得生。又說：觸為受緣。又說：能生作意為因，生所生識。此中非眼等是眼識等生因，亦非觸是受生因，非能生作意是所生識生因，由彼諸法各自種子為生因故。何故此中，說眼等為眼識等因？當知此依俱有依攝引發因說，非生起因。所以者何？由俱有眼等根為依止故，眼等諸識彼彼境轉，非無依止。
items.en: With respect to suchness and the meaning of the truths... or because of self-deprecation. No further deciding-discernment text on the remaining links appears here. Moreover, as the Blessed One said: the eye is cause, form is condition, and eye-consciousness arises; down through the body being cause, touch being condition, and body-consciousness arising. Here, the eye and the rest are not actually the generating cause of eye-consciousness and the rest, since every dharma's own individual seed is its generating cause. Why, then, is the eye and the rest here called the cause of eye-consciousness and the rest? It should be known that this speaks according to the inducing cause included within the co-existing support, not the generating cause. Why is this so? Because, in dependence on the co-existing eye faculty and the rest as support, the eye-consciousness and the rest turn towards their respective objects; they do not arise without such support.

items.zh: 如是由俱有觸為依止故，有諸受轉；由俱有能生作意為依止故。所生識轉，非無依止。是故世尊於此諸處，依俱有依所攝引發因說，非生起因。或依助伴因說。何以故？

items.title: Section: Four Sequences Through Which a Single Life Unfolds — Fascicle Sixty's Own Close

items.zh: 非已滅眼能為已生眼識所依，耳等亦爾。非已滅觸能為已生受所依止，亦非已滅能生作意能為已生所生識依。復次，緣起次第略有四種。一、牽引次第，二、生起次第，三、受用境界次第，四、受用苦次第。無明緣行、行緣識，是牽引次第。識緣名色、名色緣六處，是生起次第。六處緣觸、觸緣受，是生起已受用境界次第。受緣愛、愛緣取、取緣有、有緣生、生緣老死，是受用苦次第。於此處所餘決擇文，更不復現。
items.en: A past, already-ceased eye cannot serve as support for an already-arisen eye-consciousness, and likewise for the ear and the rest. A past, already-ceased contact cannot serve as support for an already-arisen feeling, nor can a past, already-ceased generating attention serve as support for an already-arisen consciousness. Moreover, the sequence of dependent origination is, in brief, of four kinds. First, the drawing-forth sequence. Second, the arising sequence. Third, the sequence of experiencing objects. Fourth, the sequence of experiencing suffering. Ignorance conditioning formations, and formations conditioning consciousness, is the drawing-forth sequence. Consciousness conditioning name-and-form, and name-and-form conditioning the six sense-bases, is the arising sequence. The six sense-bases conditioning contact, and contact conditioning feeling, is the sequence of experiencing objects once arisen. Feeling conditioning craving, craving conditioning clinging, clinging conditioning existence, existence conditioning birth, and birth conditioning old age and death, is the sequence of experiencing suffering. On this point, no further deciding-discernment text appears here.

blocks.text: What ignorance actually does, with a famous image: a torch whirled in a circle looks like a wheel of fire.

Master Cháng Bǎi: confusion about what is not directly seen, and ten others. From beginningless eons one has not understood the four truths or the absence of self; self-view arises on the aggregates, and from it the rest.

Master Cháng Bǎi: looking only at appearances and grasping marks wrongly is confusion of perception; a torch whirled round looks like a wheel, though no wheel exists. Some foolishness is so firm that even the Buddha's teaching does not change it; seeing others age, the fool does not expect to age.
Master Cháng Bǎi: ignorance keeps a practitioner from the first ground. Covered by desire, the mind is wholly dark; even in the formless realm a film remains.

Master Cháng Bǎi: each thing's own seed is its generating cause; but seeds alone are not enough, and the eye is needed as a co-existing support. (Untranslated, 0637c25: feeling arises with contact as support, consciousness with attention; the Buddha spoke of these as supporting causes, not generating causes.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: seeds of karma planted in the store-consciousness draw the ripened result; from name-and-form, the six bases arise.
Karma weighed: what makes it grave, light, certain, or uncertain, and how it shapes even the world outside us. Then ignorance again, "a wheel of fire that is only a torch."

quiz.q: What is ignorance's function, how many, and what are inferior, middle, and superior?
options: blocking all good, five kinds; three grades of persons, unrelated to realms
confusion about eleven matters; these match the three realms
four, about the truths; the three vehicles
three, about times; the three times
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: confusion about the not-directly-seen plus ten others make eleven functions of ignorance; inferior, middle, and superior mean the desire, form, and formless realms. The English "realms" follows that reading.

quiz.q: The English has "any object known through form or sound." What is wrong with knower and known?
options: no problem: one knows through form and sound, deficiency meaning lacking them, unrelated to faculties
the problem is "any"
form and sound are known objects, the eye and ear the knowers; the English makes objects the channel
the problem is "foolish"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with a faculty lacking, one cannot directly see form and the like, and without seeing or hearing one cannot understand. The eye and ear are the means, form and sound the objects. The English inverts that relation.

quiz.q: What are intrinsic and attachment foolishness?
options: low innate intelligence; stubborn temperament, personality matters, unrelated to truths or outsiders
lacking an eye; an ear
distraction; derangement
from beginningless time not knowing truths and no-self; fallen among outsiders, not grasping self-view
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from beginningless eons one has not understood the four truths or the no-self of beings and phenomena; on the aggregates self-view arises, and from it the sixty-two views. Note that the English rightly has "selflessness of beings and dharmas."

quiz.q: What examples does Master Cháng Bǎi give for the four confusions?
options: losing one's way in four directions, a travel example
wrong grasping of marks; a whirled torch seen as a wheel; functions imagined
four mental illnesses
four kinds of dream
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: looking only at appearances and grasping marks wrongly is perceptual confusion; a torch whirled round looks like a wheel of fire, though no wheel exists; functional confusion takes as existing what does not. The English "dimensional" for 形量 fits the torch.

quiz.q: What marks firm, excessive, and direct-perception foolishness?
options: a strong body, old age, and good eyesight, conditions of the foolish, unrelated to the Dharma
not even buddhas uproot it; knowing and doing it anyway; seeing others' ageing and not one's own
all can be uprooted by buddhas
all belong to higher realms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: such foolishness is so firm even the Buddha's teaching does not change it; the excessively foolish add more and knowingly offend; seeing others age, sicken, and die, one does not know one shares that nature. The English "in the face of direct perception" is apt.

quiz.q: In which five places does ignorance obstruct?
options: the first five perfections, wisdom being ignorance's antidote
joy of true wisdom, cessation, completing the path, good destinies, present auspiciousness
the five sense faculties
the five aggregates
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ignorance keeps a practitioner from joining the suchness of the two emptinesses, and from entering the first ground of joy; it obstructs the virtue of severance. So 真實智喜 is the joy of the first ground. The English is literal.

quiz.q: §31 has "the first three kinds... Only the last." Why can this not be understood from the English alone?
options: it is clear: the three terms at the start and the last, nothing missing, unrelated to deeds or shame
"kinds" should be "realms"
"foolish" should be "wise"
the source has four cases, the English only the first, so the terms point at nothing; the fool does wrong without shame
quiz.why: The source has four cases, of which three are absent. Master Cháng Bǎi: dwelling in latent ignorance means seeds hidden, no deed yet; one the Buddha calls a fool does wrong without remorse; being seduced by delusion means lacking shame. So "the first three" needs the lost text.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain darkness, dimness, and cataract ignorance, and what is ignorance's fruit?
options: night, dusk, and dawn, a daily cycle unrelated to realms, the fruit being only ageing and death
desire covers mind wholly; the formless still has a film, holding this mind as self; the fruit is the later links
all of the desire realm
all of the formless realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: covered by desire, the mind is wholly dark; though the formless realm is free for a time from clinging to the body, a film remains, clinging to this thought-moment as self; all eleven subsequent links are ignorance's fruit. The English "cataract" for 翳 is excellent.

quiz.q: In "the eye is cause, form condition," why is the eye not the generating cause?
options: each dharma's own seed is its generating cause; the eye is an inducing cause within co-existing support
form is the true cause, the sūtra's terms to be swapped, consciousness arising from objects, unrelated to seeds
eye-consciousness has no cause
the eye is unconditioned
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: each dharma's own seed is the generating cause; seeds alone do not suffice, and the eye is needed as co-existing support; the rest are helping conditions. A central Yogācāra point. Portions on contact and attention are lost from the Chinese and English here.

quiz.q: How do the four sequences match the twelve links?
options: ignorance to feeling draws forth, craving onward arises
all drawing-forth
all experiencing suffering
drawing-forth; arising; experiencing objects; experiencing suffering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeds of the three kinds of karma habituated in the store-consciousness draw the ripened result; from name-and-form the six bases gradually arise; craving, clinging, and existence are the causes of experiencing suffering, and birth and ageing its fruit. The English is exact.
